paragraphs: Here's what Moses wants Israel to get, friend. God didn't open with a rule. He opened with who He is: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery." (Deuteronomy 5:6) The commands come from the One who already rescued them, so they're not a pile of orders from a stranger. I know a little about being pulled out of the dark, and when somebody does that for you, you listen to what they say next.

And Moses says this covenant isn't their fathers' story. "He did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with all of us who are alive here today." (Deuteronomy 5:3) That means God's Word is never just something that happened to somebody else back then. It's spoken to whoever is standing there hearing it, and that's you, baker. Then look at God's own wish: "If only they had such a heart to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it might be well with them and with their children forever." (Deuteronomy 5:29)

So the point isn't just to hear it, it's to live it. Moses says, "Learn them and observe them carefully." (Deuteronomy 5:1) Why? "So that you may live and prosper and prolong your days in the land that you will possess." (Deuteronomy 5:33) God's way is where life is, so take it all in, friend, and let it shape how you walk. And Moses is NOT done talking, so stay in your chair, because this teaching keeps going.
